audience: Undergraduate students with no electrochemistry background; curious but easily lost by jargon.
objective: Build a working mental model of why solid-state batteries matter, ending in one clear takeaway.
sourcePack: Liquid electrolytes are flammable organic solvents; dendrites pierce separators; solid ceramic separators block dendrites physically; sulfides conduct 12.5 mS/cm vs liquids ~10 mS/cm (comparable); manufacturing (cold-pressing stacks) is the open hard problem, not chemistry alone.
requiredClaims: Liquid electrolytes can burn; solids remove that fuel
Manufacturing, not raw conductivity, is the open problem
forbiddenClaims: Solid-state batteries are already in mass production
Jargon without explanation (mS/cm must be grounded)
requiredEvidence: a mechanical intuition for dendrite blocking
nuance: Motivation before mechanism; every number needs an intuition anchor. A deck that front-loads figures fails.
